articleTitle: "Under the big sky" - Optical MEMS - August 2006
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.

articleTitle: Free-space MEMS tunable optical filter on [110] silicon
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Tunable optical filters (TOFs) are key components in optical communication WDM networks. In this paper we have successfully demonstrated two-Bragg mirror Fabry-Perot MEMS tunable optical filter fabrication by a combination of KOH and deep reactive ion etching in (110) silicon

articleTitle: Continuous optical sorting of HeLa cells and microparticles using optoelectronic tweezers
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate an automatic optical sorting technique that combines video image analysis, pattern recognition, and adaptive optoelectronic tweezers (OET) actuation on a continuously moving chip. This tool is capable of sorting cells and particles according to their visual characteristics at the single-cell level

articleTitle: A laser display using a PZT-actuated 2D optical scanner
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report an image projection display using a MEMS 2D optical scanner driven by the PZT unimorph actuators developed by the ADRIP method. Improved contrast ratio of optical scan speeds with relatively large angles (horizontal: optical 27 degrees at 16.4 kHz, vertical: optical 31 degrees at 77.4 Hz, frequency ratio of 210) has made it possible to project monotone bitmap animations

articleTitle: Two-axis MEMS scanner for display and imaging applications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Two-axis gimbaled scanner used in an SVGA display product with 58deg optical scan angle, 1.5 mm mirror size, and 21 KHz resonant frequency is reported. Scanner is actuated electromagnetically using a single coil on the outer frame and by mechanical coupling of outer frame motion into the inner mirror frame

articleTitle: Optical MEMS for advanced spectrometers
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Optical MEMS based spectrometers capable to perform time resolved measurements from VIS to NIR are presented. They are based on high frequency scanning gratings with V-groove-structure and translational mirrors for Fourier-transform-spectrometers, respectively

articleTitle: Low-temperature LD direct bonding for highly functional optical MEMS
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper reports the results of low-temperature flip-chip bonding of a vertical cavity surface emitting laser (VCSEL) on a micromachined Si substrate. Low temperature bonding was achieved by introducing surface activation by plasma irradiation into the flip-chip bonding process. After the surfaces of the Au electrodes of the VCSEL and Si substrate were cleaned using an Ar radio frequency (RF) plasma, Au-Au bonding was carried out only by contact in ambient air. At a bonding temperature of 100 degC, the die-shear strength exceeded the failure criteria of MIL-STD-883

articleTitle: Tunable, membrane-based, pneumatic micro-mirrors
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A novel design of tunable, membrane-based micro-mirrors is presented. The micro-mirror is actuated by pneumatic pressure which provides large deflection and a large range of angle from -10deg to 70deg, relative to the substrate surface

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of a MEMS 1-D optical scanner using self-assembled vertical combs and scan-angle magnifying mechanism
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report a novel one-axis MEMS optical scanner with a scan-angle magnifying mechanism. Small actuator-motion was amplified through the two-mass-two-spring mechanism, and a large mirror angle was obtained

articleTitle: An in-plane dispersive system utilizing micro tunable vertical grating
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A miniaturized tunable dispersive optical system is presented, which consisted of a novel tunable vertical grating operated in the visible. Preliminary results for fabricating and testing such device are also conducted to prove the feasibility

articleTitle: A new approach for focusing deformable mirrors fabricated in polymer technology
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Nowadays, adaptive optics are already being used in a broad range of applications. The growing market of applications demands for low-cost adaptive optics with high optical quality. Adaptive optics like deformable mirrors, fabricated using micro structure technologies, currently cost about 60 USD. In this work, a circular adaptive mirror device for laser focussing was developed and fabricated in polymer materials. The focal length can be varied within the range from 0.1 to 1 m. Besides the cost-efficient fabrication of the mirror device this concept also features only one actuator for focussing. The driving voltage of the actuator lies in the range of 0 to 12 V, depending on the focal length of the deformable mirror

articleTitle: Development of two dimensional scanner-on-scanner for confocal laser scanning microscope "LEXT" series
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A two dimensional (2-D) Scanner-on-scanner (SOS) has been developed for commercial confocal laser scanning microscope (LSM) "LEXT' series. The SOS consists of a newly developed electromagnetic MEMS scanner mounted on a commercially available galvanometric scanner, being inclined at 45deg. The SOS realizes much smaller distortion in the 2-D scanning pattern than that obtained by gimbaled type MEMS 2-D scanner. Key issue is miniaturizing the MEMS scanner so that it can be mounted onto the galvanometric scanner. It was realized by using a coil for both driving and sensing so that sensing output was increased, and thus size reduction of permanent magnets have become possible, leading to the scanner volume of approximately 9.3 % of the one previously developed for a LSM, Olympus OLS1200

articleTitle: Dynamic characterization of MEMS-tunable vertical-cavity SOAs
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We analyze the dynamics of tunable-VCSOAs. At 6 mT the devices exhibit a Q of ~500 and an f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> of 168.32 kHz. At atmosphere Q is reduced to 1.2 resulting in <10 mus switching times

articleTitle: MEMS compatible micro-GRIN lenses for in plane beam manipulation
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: The design, simulation, fabrication and characterization of micro-GRIN lenses with a diameter of 125 mum is presented. GRIN rods having the same diameter as optical fibers can be passively aligned using U-grooves and microfabricated springs

articleTitle: Organic variable optical attenuator made by compliant fluoropolymer membrane
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: The paper describes the design and fabrication of micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) variable optical attenuator (VOA) made by a compliant organic thin film. The optical attenuation is achieved by changing the radius of curvature of the organic thin film actuated by the electrostatic force. The simulation results show that the attenuation range can achieve 20 dB at the wavelength of 1550 nm

articleTitle: Electrostatic micro-shutter array for infrared spectrograph
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report an electrostatic micro shutter array for astronomical telescopes for parallel processing infrared spectroscopy of multiple celestial objects using bulk-micromachining of silicon-on-insulator wafers. Successful operation of micro torsion shutter to a 90-degree-deflection has been demonstrated with applied voltages of up to 95 V DC

articleTitle: MEMS-based high-speed low-power vector display
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a MEMS-based vector display system utilizing gimbal-less two-axis micromirror scanners for high-speed laser beam-steering. The system is capable of displaying freehand sketches, parametric curves, text, as well as multiframe animations at arbitrary refresh rates. The scanners can be operated in point-to-point vector scanning or resonant and rastering modes. Due to ultra-low power consumption of the MEMS devices, the system is highly portable, miniature and powered and controlled via a PC USB interface

articleTitle: Electrostatically controlled transparent display pixels by PEN-films MEMS
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a low-cost transparent display pixel using the MEMS electrostatic Fabry-Perot interferometer. A thin plastic sheet of polyethylene naphthalate was laminated over a glass substrate with an optical cavity, and the electrostatic deformation of the film controlled the color of transmitting light. Color change between dark-white and bright green was successfully demonstrated with a 120 Vdc at a 2.2 ms response speed

articleTitle: Patterned gas absorbing films for assuring long-term reliability and improving performances of mems and omems
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Microsensor packaging is one of the most important and challenging technology areas. Many microelectro-mechanical systems (MEMS) and optical MEMS (OMEMS) need to be protected from outside environment stresses: therefore the package must provide an interior environment compatible with the device operation, performances, reliability and lifetime. In addition some MEMS need a specific gas or pressure environment within the package to operate as specified: in particular, OMEMS should be protected against moisture related failures

articleTitle: A modular custom aperture technology for optimization of MEMS scanners
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: In this work a MEMS based, customizable aperture size, beam steering technology is demonstrated. Sets of electrostatic actuators optimized for speed, angle, area footprint or resonant driving are designed and realized in a self-aligned DRIE fabrication process. Scanning mirrors exhibiting fast point-to-point, or resonant, scanning speeds and high resolution are critical elements in a diverse; range of application areas including: optical communications, medical imaging, adaptive optics, LIDAR systems and displays. In most cases, designers trade off among three primary parameters: speed, aperture size, and angle. A given set of design trade offs may be possible in a specialized MEMS technology, however, this same set of trade offs will most likely not satisfy the requirements for other applications. A modular approach to MEMS scanner design is required in order to effectively address this problem. Namely, the system designer would ideally want to choose from a set of available actuators and mirrors to attain a desired parameter space for their application

articleTitle: Infrared detection of carbon monoxide with a micromechanically tunable silicon fabry-perot filter
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Robust sensing of carbon monoxide is possible with a tunable correlation filter. We demonstrate a silicon Fabry-Perot filter with high optical throughput, where an adjustable hidden airgap allows for the necessary tuning

articleTitle: A surface emitting solid polymer dye laser using a guided mode resonant grating for bio-optical detections
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A new surface emitting dye laser is proposed for bio-optical detections in micro-TAS. The micro laser consists of a guided mode resonant grating made of dye doped PMMA. In an arbitrary area where the sub-wavelength grating is patterned, single-mode laser oscillation is obtained at the wavelength determined by the grating period

articleTitle: Tunable microcavities in two dimensional photonic crystal waveguides
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: In this work, we investigate the transmission properties of tunable resonant cavities inside photonic crystal waveguides. We present an optical and a mechanical way of perturbing the optical environment near the resonant cavity enabling tuning and modulation of the in-plane transmission. We have discussed different ways that change the transmission properties of cavities in photonic crystals. Optical switching and wavelength tuning is obtainable by means of induced thermo and electro optical effects. These results indicate the feasibility of high-speed optical integrated circuits based on silicon photonic crystal structures. In addition, simulations have shown that an AFM tip can be used for tuning and damping. These results suggest a stand-alone MEMS solution to create a chip-based on-off switch or tunable filter. Furthermore, one could attempt to integrate more than one silicon tip to combine filter and tuning functionalities on one device. By separately controlling the position of the different tips a programmable integrated optical circuit with higher integration density and functionality could be achieved

articleTitle: Spherical aberration correction using a silicon nitride deformable membrane mirror
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A gold-coated silicon nitride membrane mirror 1.25 mm in diameter corrects up to 3 waves of spherical aberration at 633 nm. A 2times improvement in edge response is observed in an N.A. 0.55 optical system

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of MEMS optical modulators integrated with PHC waveguides
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report the design and fabrication process of MEMS actuators for optical attenuators integrated with two-dimensional photonic crystal waveguide. Fabrication process has been improved from our previous model such that the SOI PhC layer is not delaminated during the sacrificial release in HF. The device was successfully developed and optically tested to obtain 2 dB modulation contrast at an 86 V with -27 dB insertion loss

articleTitle: High fill-factor micromirror array and its fabrication process
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: The micromirror array with high fill-factor of 91% is fabricated. For high fill-factor, the posts supporting the mirror plate are filled up with copper by the uniform electroplating process

articleTitle: Silicon-based tunable liquid lens system
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a novel silicon-based micro-lens system actuated by electro-wetting including a lens centering mechanism and taking advantage of silicon dioxide dielectric layers and low surface roughness of standard MEMS-processes

articleTitle: Micro-encoder using image obtained by ball lens assembled inside wafer
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: An absolute micro-encoder based on the code imaging is developed. The ball lens (phi300 mum) is assembled inside the cavity between the pyrex glass lid and suspensions in the handling Si layer of the SOI wafer. The photodiode array is prepared in the device Si layer. The image of the scale is incident on the backside of the photodiodes. The electrical wiring to photodiodes does not disturb the optics. The current signal shows the sufficient contrast for resolving the maximum length code having the minimum line width of 13.6 mum

articleTitle: Microfabricated atomic clocks and magnetometers
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate the critical subsystems of compact atomic clocks and magnetometers based on microfabricated physics packages. The clock components have a volume below 5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, a fractional frequency instability below 6times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup>tau<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>, and consume 200 mW of power. The magnetometer has a sensitivity below 40pT/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> at 50 Hz

articleTitle: Performance of tense thin film torsion bar for large-rotation and low-voltage driving of micromirror
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A micromirror device is developed realizing the large-rotation and the low-voltage driving (obtained maximum value is 8.6 degrees at 5 V). The thin film torsion bars, which consist of SiN and Au/Cr films, contribute to this performance. Inside the torsion bar, the tension is included for generating the compliance in the mirror rotation and stiffness in other movements. The performance of the torsion bar is investigated

articleTitle: A reconfigurable add-drop filter using mems-actuated microdisk resonator
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A novel vertically coupled tunable microdisk resonator with integrated MEMS tunable optical couplers is demonstrated. A reconfigurable add-drop filter based on this device shows an extinction ratio of 20 dB

articleTitle: Vernier MOEMS alignment mechanisms
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Positional precision in MOEMS alignment is increased beyond the value set by pattern transfer using a Vernier mechanism based on multiple rack-and-tooth latches. Two- and four-section latches are demonstrated, and limits in precision magnification identified

articleTitle: Measurement and calculation of laser beam spot distortion caused by dynamic deformation of scanning mirror
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report the measurement and calculation results of a laser beam spot distortion caused by dynamic deformation of a MEMS scanning mirror. The laser beam spot distortion is measured by using the CCD camera located on focal point when an emission timing of the laser beam is synchronized with a motion of the scanning mirror. The calculated distortion is simulated by using the Fresnel-Kirchhoff diffraction formula. A dynamic deformation of the mirror is calculated by FEM. Their results have showed good agreement. Therefore we have proved our calculation method available

articleTitle: High-speed optical nanofabrication by platinum oxide nano-explosion - all dry-fabrication
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Using nano-explosion of platinum oxide thin film, 50-nm pit pattern was optically fabricated optically at linear speed of 3.0 m/s. We achieved the patterning speed of 15 million pits/s and actually fabricated the huge numbers of the pit

articleTitle: MOEMS laser tuning element with an indirect drive
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A tuning element for a Littrow external cavity laser combining a vertically etched blazed grating and linear and rotary tuning actuators is demonstrated. Extended tuning is achieved using an indirect drive via a flexure

articleTitle: Gravure printed optoelectronic thin films for flexible polymer LEDS and microsystems
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Polymer LEDs based on gravure printed light-emitting polymer film were investigated. The printed films achieved flat uniformity over large area given a capability of roll-to-roll manufacturing of optoelectrical thin film components

articleTitle: Design, fabrication and characterization of a novel electrostatically actuated optical fiber switch
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We will present the design, modeling, simulation, fabrication and characterization of a novel fiber optical switch that fulfils all requirements of optical measurement applications. The optical fiber switch presented here moves one incoming fiber with respect to two outgoing fibers. Our new approach moves fibers directly by electrostatic actuation within an "actuation chamber". A detailed modeling of the transient fiber movement under electrostatic load was done with FE methods

articleTitle: Development of small port-count ROADM using MEMS type 2x2 OSWs and VOAs
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We developed a low cost small port-count ROADM(Reconfigurable Optical Add-Drop Multiplexer) using simple MEMS (Micro Electro-Mechanical System) type 2times2 OSWs (Optical Switches) and VOAs (variable optical attenuators). The ROADM module consisting of components all developed in-house performed fast and reliable add/drop function with channel equalisation. The output power flatness was controlled to less than 0.5 dB over four CWDM channels

articleTitle: MEMS tunable fabry-perot optical filter
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Fabry-Perot (FP) optical filter is an interface reflection mode device selecting only the resonance wavelength and ignoring others within the mirror stop-band. The transmitted wavelength can be tuned by varying the optical path length of the FP cavity. We investigate the wavelength tuning limits that can be obtained by using MEMS concept

articleTitle: Application of phase locking loop control for mems resonant devices
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: The phase locking control method to ensure the operating of MEMS actuators at their resonant frequency is presented. In this study, the control algorithm was simulated by the MATLAB. Further, an optical scanner fabricated using the SOI wafer was employed to demonstrate the present technique. Thus the variation of the scanning angle resulted from the offset of the natural frequency of the devices can be prevented

articleTitle: Long-wavelength MEMS tunable VCSEL with high sidemode suppression
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Singlemode emission exceeding 1 mW over 28 nm tuning range of an electrically pumped long-wavelength VCSEL is achieved. A tunable curved MEMS Bragg mirror enables high output power operation with sidemode suppression of more than 40 dB

articleTitle: Atomic force microscopy with optical heterodyne detection method
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report on an atomic force microscope (AFM) based on a simple optical set-up using heterodyne detection. The deflection of the cantilever in the AFM was interferometrically measured using a Michelson interferometer. At a scanning speed of 2 mum/s and an integration time of 10 ms, the measured vertical resolution was 0.4 nm. The lateral resolution was 20 nm and is determined by the scanning speed and the integration time

articleTitle: Variable optical delay prototype using a 2d array of mems mirrors
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A variable optical signal delay is desirable for TDM optical networks and optical beamforming in phased-array antennas. A MEMS device with 2-bit variable delay for optical signals is proposed. The design of a device to introduce this controllable delay will have to use moveable mirrors that physically change the path of the optical signal

articleTitle: A physically based model for dielectric charging in an integrated optical mems wavelength selective switch
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A physical parameter based model for dielectric charge accumulation is proposed and used to predict the displacement versus applied voltage and pull-in response of an electrostatic MEMS wavelength selective integrated optical switch

articleTitle: Optical properties and applications of porous silicon
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: The paper summarizes the optical properties of porous silicon membranes synthesized by anodic etching of p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> Si wafers. The dependence of optical properties on the structural parameters-determined by the experimental conditions-is emphasized; and the potential applications of porous silicon are presented

articleTitle: Silicon masking layers for fabrication of high aspect ratio MEMS
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a fabrication technique for high-aspect ratio MEMS using a planar silicon layer bonded to a structured substrate. The bonded silicon layer provides a flat surface that can be patterned by conventional photolithography. These patterns are then transferred to the substrate through a series of etch steps. The bonded silicon layer is etched together with the substrate, so the use of additional silicon masking layers, followed by patterning and etching, can be repeated as many times as necessary. Using this approach, we have successfully demonstrated vertical mirror fabrication by a combination of KOH and DRIE etching in (110) silicon

articleTitle: A simple process to fabricate self-aligned, high-performance torsional microscanners; demonstrated use in a two-dimensional scanner
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: CMOS-compatible process carried out on SOI wafers, we have built high-performance torsional microscanners having vertically offset interdigitated-comb actuators. Our microscanner-fabrication process requires three photolithography masks: two to form the front-side microscanner structures and a third to define the backside openings. Both moving and fixed combs are fabricated in the same device layer (30 mum in thickness), and the offset combs are created by reducing the thickness of the fixed combs, but not that of the moving combs. Our process begins by removing the 1-mum thick thermal oxide selectively to open rectangular windows at locations where the fixed combs are to be defined. In the following step, both fixed- and moving-comb sets are defined simultaneously with a single photolithography mask; this is followed by deep-reactive ion etching (DRIE). We then perform a tuned-etch in the DRIE-etcher to obtain the desired vertical thickness for the fixed combs without affecting the moving combs. The minimum gap between comb fingers can be as small as twice the alignment accuracy of the photolithography process, which is les0.4 mum for state-of-the-art photolithography steppers. We consider these microscanners as especially well adapted for applications to refractive laser surgery of ocular corneas where small spot size and high scan speeds are important assets

articleTitle: Micro-actuated small-scale spherical retroreflector for free space optical communications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper describes the use of electrothermal MEMS actuation and small-scale spherical retroreflectors to produce a retroreflective optical phase modulator

articleTitle: Bioactive hybrid materials for photonic microsysterns
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Bioactive hybrid materials have been produced by the sol-gel method. Antibodies used in this work retained their activity after doping and processing. The developed materials can be used e.g. for optical MEMS applications in diagnostics

articleTitle: 3-D MEMS based real-time minimally invasive endoscopic optical coherence tomography
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A 3-dimensional, endoscopic optical coherence tomography (OCT) system based on a high-speed micromachined scanning mirror is presented. Cross sectional images of in-vitro and in-vivo samples are obtained and continuously displayed to the user. The optical resolution of the system is approximately 20 mumtimes20 mumtimes10 mum. The endoscopic OCT probe has been utilized to identify cancerous regions of hamster cheek pouch tissue in real-time

articleTitle: Integrated tracking and focusing systems in a monolithic device for MEMS optical pick-up head
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: This work proposed a novel optical pickup head with tracking and focusing system in a monolithic device. The device was fabricated by poly-Si trench-refilled technology and used UV polymer droplet as objective lens. In-plane (tracking) and out-of-plane (focusing) motion were decoupled by springs, gimbal structure, and actuators. In results, we successfully demonstrate the proposed device included single tracking system, single focusing, and integrated system. The resonant frequency of tacking and focusing systems are 9.6 kHz and 4.2 kHz respectively

articleTitle: Vision-based teleoperation of a stroboscopic microscopic interferownetric system for remote dynamic MEMS testing
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We demonstrate a system that automatically locates MEMS structures under a microscope equipped with a 3 DOF stage. It correlates images directly with the chip-mask layout and is especially useful for teleoperated experiments

articleTitle: Deformable mems grating for wide tunability
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A deformable MEMS grating is presented. Electrostatic actuation allows a per cent tuning of up to 2.5%. This device can be used as tuning element in an external cavity mid-infrared quantum-cascade laser

articleTitle: A low voltage two-step micromirror for the pinhole of the confucal microscope
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, a novel electrostatic two-step micromirror which can serve as a pinhole and be driven at low voltages is presented. We have designed, fabricated and tested the two-step micromirror. It has a novel structure with an intermediate moving plate. The fabricated device has successfully demonstrated the reduction of the driving voltage. The proposed micromirror can be used in low voltage optical applications such as in-vivo endoscopic biopsy

articleTitle: Spectrometer based on MOEMS shutter array
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: In this work a MOEMS shutter array was developed to be a wavelength selective component inside the spectrometer. This paper presents the implemented spectrometer prototype based on the MOEMS shutter array

articleTitle: Thermally actuated micro scanner for barcode reader applications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost 1D thermally actuated silicon micro scanner developed for our industrial partner. It was designed and optimised for mass production. With a really simple and standard fabrication process we obtained a high yield (> 95%) and good reproducibility of the scanner characteristics: low resonance frequency, good shock resistance, low power consumption, easy control, large mechanical sweep angle and a flat reflective surface

articleTitle: Imaging micro-spectrometer with adaptive space-variant dispersion
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A space-variant variable-dispersion imaging micro-spectrometer is described. An array of MEMs mirrors is used to select different optical paths through the spectrometer, permitting dynamically adjustable grating dispersion on a pixel-by-pixel basis across the image. Diffraction-limited performance is achieved across the 500-1000 nm wavelength range; and spectral resolutions ranging from 5 to 20 nm

articleTitle: Optical actuation of mems micro-gears through radiation pressure
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: The optical processes involved in laser trapping and optical manipulation are explored as a means of actuating micron-sized gear structures. It is shown that laser trapping can be used to suspend in 3-D polyimide gears and set them into rotation. Subsequently we present the light actuation of micron-sized gear structures fabricated with a polysilicon surface micro-machining technique

articleTitle: Periodic rib-reinforced silicon nitride scan mirrors
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Uniaxial scan mirrors measuring 1500 um in diameter were fabricated from a 1.4 um thick rib-reinforced silicon nitride film. The structurally enhanced film minimized surface deformation due to internal stress and inertial effects during actuation

articleTitle: Dispersion compensation in cpw-based optical modulators and photo detectors using mems technology
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A MEMS tunable optical coplanar waveguide (CPW) based modulator/ photo-detector is introduced. It could apply phase and amplitude corrections at both ends of an optical link, potentially reducing the inter symbol interference (ISI) caused by dispersive effects

articleTitle: Microdevices for high resolution measurement
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We summarize two on-going projects: suspended microchannel resonator for biomolecular detection and scanning probe microscopy with inherent disturbance suppression. The microfabricated devices with optical readout are used for high resolution measurement

articleTitle: Zoom camera based on variable-focus liquid lenses
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A zoom camera was constructed based on two adjustable lenses. The strongly varying lens shapes make an achromatic design complicated. Special liquids are required to prevent chromatic aberrations for all zoom levels and object positions

articleTitle: Optical power-scavenging system for fluidic microsensors
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: An extremely compact optical power-scavenging system is presented providing onboard power for an autonomous remote metal-ion sensor. The total volume of the sensor system including power supply is below 0.046 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and with a short circuit current of 0.51 muA under sunlight conditions. To the authors' knowledge this is the smallest autonomous micromachined power supply and device ever built

articleTitle: Roll-to-roll manufacturing technologies for flexible MEMS applications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Roll-to-roll fabrication of electrical and optical structures and functional elements on web will be described. Based on the realized components, the potential of the printing techniques for volume-scale MEMS fabrication will be introduced

articleTitle: Thermally actuated MEMS optical devices
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Micromirrors with linear deflection behaviors have been found useful for systems requiring 1D and 2D optical scanning patterns and are solutions for low-cost vector or video raster image generators. The advantages of thermal buckle-beam and bimorph actuators are high resulting force, low MEMS area and low voltage requirements. The mirror devices presented in this paper can achieve modest deflection angles at relatively high frequencies. Non-resonant, near-linear 2D mirror deflection response has been achieved with a maximum deflection of 12 optical degrees at a frequency of a few KHz. Employing a high Q resonant structure, a frequency of 14 KHz has been attained with a 1D mirror scanner at a maximum optical deflection of around 40 degrees. 1D and 2D scanning mirror devices have been built and improved and will be reviewed in this paper. A tunable Bragg defraction grating will also be discussed

articleTitle: Opto-plasmonic tweezers for rotation and manipulation of micro/nano objects
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a new opto-plasmonic tweezer for trapping and fine orientation control of micro/nano objects. The device utilizes polarized light to excite resonant dipoles on the surface of an Au nanoparticle array. The large dielectrophoresis force is then created by the highly non-uniform optically induced dipole field. The orientation control is realized by adjusting the polarization direction of the incident light. Theoretical modeling, preliminary fabrication and experimental results are reported

articleTitle: Micro polarizing beam splitter for blue wavelength optical pickups application
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Micro polarizing beam splitters (micro PBS) are required in micro optical systems for sensing and signal processing when the polarization state is a concern. In this paper, silicon nitride thin films with low stress and low absorption at 405 nm wavelength were investigated. The reflectance and the transmittance of TM and TE modes of a pop-up micro-PBS composed of a silicon nitride thin film and a poly-silicon frame were examined. Two types of micro PBSs based on low stress silicon nitride were successfully demonstrated. The performance agreed well with calculation. Such devices can be applied for micro optical pickups in data storage systems

articleTitle: Frequency conversion using photonic crystals and NEMS/MEMS
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose combining a photonic crystal and nano-electro-mechanical systems (NEMS) to produce significant optical frequency conversion by modulating the resonant cavity dimensions with the NEMS. Simulation results predict a 25% frequency shift

articleTitle: Micromechanical actuators for spectroscopic measurements
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, advantages of surface micromachined silicon devices as parallel-moving planar actuators are described. These devices are especially intended for interferometric applications, such as Fourier transform spectroscopy (FTS). FTS has become a widely-used, high-precision method for analytical chemistry greatly because of its wide range of operation from UV to sub-millimeter wavelengths

articleTitle: Fabrication and test of square prism shaped dye micro laser based on photoresist molding process
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A dielectric microcavity of dye doped polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) is fabricated by SU-8 photoresist molding technique. The molding technique by fabricating a solid polymer dye microcavity laser is described in detail. The dye laser microcavity resonators properties are confirmed

articleTitle: Bell labs nanotechnologies: devices for the terabit communications networks of the future
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Nanotechnology is the emerging field, which will impact almost every area of science and technology. In areas as diverse as the chemical, automotive, aeronautical, cellular, optical communications industries as well as basic science, nanotechnology is becoming the solution of choice for many problems. In this talk I will describe what the devices are, how they are built and show how they have the potential to revolutionize many application areas. I will show examples of these devices and describe some of the challenges in attacking the billions of dollars in addressable markets for this technology

articleTitle: Direct optical biosensor based on optical feedback interferometry
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, MEMs solution of the biosensor based on optical feedback interferometry is presented. Optical feedback occurs when part of the emitted laser light is coupled back into the laser cavity. The light interacts with the original laser light producing an interference signal which is detected using a photodetector placed on the opposite side of the laser cavity

articleTitle: Requirements of deformable mirrors for adaptive optics
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: An adaptive optics (AO) system is one that is capable of correcting dynamic distortions and aberrations in an optical image or beam. There are three keys elements in a "conventional" AO system: the wavefront sensor, the correction device ("deformable mirror", DM), and a control system. The fundamental limits of AO are usually governed by the noise in the wavefront sensor, but the practical limit is often set by the correction device. Possible correction devices include: piezo-stack mirrors, bimorph mirrors, membrane mirrors, MEMS mirrors and refractive or reflective liquid crystal spatial light modulators. The temporal response required of deformable mirrors is strongly application dependent, varying from perhaps a few Hz in vision science to several KHz in strong turbulence. A parameter of special significance when thinking about MEMS mirrors is the physical size of the device. The DM is placed in a plane conjugate to the plane of the aberration (this might be the pupil plane in some cases), and the ratio of the diameter of the device to that of the correction area (e.g. pupil) determines the (de-)magnification M: however, angles in the pupil are then magnified by a factor M on the DM

articleTitle: A 2d optical lens scanner with small footprint actuators
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper proposes a new optical and mechanical design for an optical crossconnect using MEMS 2D lens scanner. Optical simulation justified the use of telescope optics for low loss and compact OXC design. The suspensions and the electrostatic mechanism were designed in separate SOI layers to compress the device footprint and to accommodate more optical channels

articleTitle: Stress mapping sensors for high power adaptive microoptics
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Directional stress and temperature effects are simultaneously measured and decoupled in micromachined membrane mirrors using a group of three ion implanted silicon resistors with different orientations. In a demonstration mirror, the sensors show compressive thermal stress changes of about -0.5plusmn0.08 MPa/degC and -0.66plusmn0.09 MPa/degC in the x and y-direction respectively

articleTitle: 1x2 MEMS optical switch with sub 10 /spl mu/s switching speed inside silicon gold coated planar hollow waveguides (PHW)
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a new approach for guided-wave optical switches based on square silicon planar hollow waveguides (PHW). A 1times2 MEMS optical switch is manufactured by inserting into the hollow planar waveguide a micromechanical cantilever beam switch at the junction of Y waveguides. The small dimension of hollow planar waveguides (20 mum wide and 20 mum deep) and of the beam (2 mum wide and 250 mum long) allow very fast switching time below 10 mus. The fabrication steps to manufacture the switch need only two masks level. Gold coating enhances reflectivity inside hollow core. Planar hollow waveguides have another great advantage in the fact that optical function such as switching can be fabricated in the same process step than the hollow waveguide. This enables the fabrication of monolithic optical functions

articleTitle: 2 DOF optical microscanner with large deflection angles
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper reports on a novel microscanner with two degrees-of-freedom (DOF) fabricated from a shape memory alloy (SMA) thin film composite consisting of a three-layer system of Ti(Ni,Cu)/Mo/Fc(Cr,Ni). This three-layer system creates concave and convex curvatures upon heating and cooling, respectively, due to a strong change of bimorph stress mainly induced by a martensitic transformation. The resulting coupled thermal, mechanical and optical performance characteristics of Ti(Ni,Cu) thin films are deposited by DC-magnetron sputtering onto unheated Mo substrates, which exhibit a lower thermal expansion coefficient compared to TiNi-based alloys

articleTitle: A tunable concave microlens with hybrid alignment in liquid crystal
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A tunable concave LC microlens was demonstrated by micro-imprinting vertical alignment polyimide on a horizontal alignment layer. The microlens functions concave and its focal length is electrically controllable

articleTitle: A linearly optical scanning mirror for real-time imaging of optical coherence tomography
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A linearly optical scanning mirror serving as the reference mirror in OCT was developed. The 3mm aperture mirror was measured to have resonant frequency of 570Hz and 768mum stroke, which enable real-time imaging of OCT

articleTitle: A multi-chip directly mounted 512 MEMS mirror array module with hermetically sealed package for large optical cross-connects
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A 512 MEMS mirror array module with a hermetically sealed package for large optical cross-connects is constructed by using newly developed multi-chip direct mounting (MCDM) technology and is demonstrated to enable a plusmn5 degree rotation of the two-axis stationary operation under a drive voltage of 160 V, while having a high resonance frequency of 2 kHz

articleTitle: High resolution optical characterization of cantilever arrays and multiple air-gap cavities for scanning probe microscopy, communication, analytics and sensing
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present an ultra-precise optical methodology to investigate complex nano- and microscale structures fabricated by micromachining. This method is applied for micromachined tunable multiple air-gap GaInAsP microresonators as well as for Si cantilever arrays which are fabricated commercially. These different devices are applied in scanning probe microscopy, analytics, sensing and high bit-rate communication. A detailed comparison of experimental studies with results of theoretical model calculations is performed on the basis of line-shape-fits to provide precise geometric and compositional parameters. We obtain an excellent agreement between experimental and theoretical data

articleTitle: Solid-immersion micromirror with enhanced angular deflection for silicon-based planar lightwave circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We report on a MEMS-based on-chip solid-immersion micromirror (SIM), which provides enhanced angular deflection and reduced diffraction loss. The SIM is driven by rotary comb-drive actuators. Maximum mechanical scan angle of 8 degree is achieved

articleTitle: OPLEAF connecting optical fibers to ifigh density optical IC
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We have designed and fabricated an OPLEAF (OPtical LEAd Frame) that serves as the interface between optical fibers and a high density optical IC. The OPLEAF is a micromachined structure for converting an optical fiber array pitch from 250 mum to 30 mum and aligning thinned fibers to the optical IC

articleTitle: Intelligent optical networks using mems based devices
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents demonstrated results of intelligent optical networks using photonics cross connect equipment. The field trial and the all-optical networking test bed confirmed that MEMS-based optical switches were validated in the carriers' actual environment

articleTitle: Honeycomb textured front surface of monocrystalline silicon and borosilicate glass substrates
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present the results of an experimental study regarding the increase of the silicon solar cells efficiency by texturing the front surface and the fabrication of microcells on borosilicate glass substrate using silicon micromachining technologies. A `honeycomb' textured front surface has been obtained using a photolithography process to generate patterns (disc hole) on the top surface followed by isotropic etching

articleTitle: Direct temperature measurement in femtoliter chamber using fluorescent dye
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Direct temperature measurement inside the micro chamber, in the order of few femtoliter in volume, is the key technology for the up coming experiments in single molecular observation. The temperature inside the cylinder shaped micro chamber, 8 mum indiameter and 2.2 mum in height, was directly detected. The temperature was calculated from the temperature dependent fluorescent intensity of Rhodamine B water solution contained inside the micro chamber

articleTitle: Materials that feel pain - distributed strain sensing by optical fibers embedded in structures and materials
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Optical fibers can act as a sensor for strain, pressure and so on, through its optical properties, such as scattering and propagation-modes coupling. By additionally applying a way to analyze distribution of these properties along the fiber, the fiber acts as nerve for materials and structures, in which the fiber is embedded. The fiber optic nerve can sense damages induced in the materials and structures. We have proposed an optical correlation domain technique with continuous lightwave. By applying the technique, for example, to fiber Brillouin distributed strain sensing, we have demonstrated 1 cm spatial resolution and 57 Hz sampling rate, which are 100 times and 104 times higher than the time domain techniques, respectively

articleTitle: Application of stand-by switching large core diameter optical fiber switch
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A 1times2 optical switch using POF/PCF and an SMA coil actuator with magnetic latches is fabricated and tested. A stand-by switch using the fabricated fiber switches is assembled and its operation is confirmed

articleTitle: Label free detection of biomolecular interactions
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: This work presents a simple evanescent wave sensing system based on an interferometric approach suitable to meet the demands on label free sensor systems for the detection of biomolecular interactions especially. It is representing a basic concept towards high throughput application. The system performance and reproducibility was evaluated with refractometric measurements of sucrose dilutions. A mean resolution of the effective refractive index of 3sigma(Deltamacrnmacr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub>)=0.9middot10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> without averaging and a reproducibility below sigma<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=0.1middot10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> were achieved. The suitability for the detection of biomolecular interactions was validated with the detection of a DNA hybridization

articleTitle: Microreplication in a silicon processing compatible polymer material
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present a novel fabrication process for the integration of polymer micro-optical elements on silicon. The process relies on a reverse order protocol based on embossing in an amorphous fluorocarbon polymer, Cytoptrade

articleTitle: A 2x2 optical add-drop module with attenuation controllability using two 45/spl deg/ movable micromirrors
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We propose a simple offset-error-free micromachined 2times2 optical add-drop module (OADM) with attenuation controllability. By the diagonal motion of two V-type micromirrors, the OADM switch controls optical paths as well as attenuation. The fabricated OADM showed insertion losses of 1.9 dB, and on/off contrast of 70 dB. The difference of the optical power between the channels was within plusmn0.1 dB for a 50 dB attenuation range. The wavelength dependent losses were less than 0.3 dB, 1.3 dB, 1.4 dB at the attenuation of initial state, 10 dB, and 20 dB, respectively

articleTitle: Mirror with two parallel rotation axes for external cavity laser
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A mirror device for an external cavity diode laser is fabricated. To achieve a wide and continuous tuning range, mechanical linkage of two parallel rotation axes can rotate and translate the mirror, generating a virtual pivot point of the mirror motion. This mirror device is realized using a wafer-folding technique

articleTitle: Piezoelectric thin-film unimorph actuator for optical fiber alignment in photonic modules
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: Feasibility of a piezoelectric PZT unimorph thin-film actuator on silicon substrates for optical fiber alignment in hybrid photonic modules was investigated. Displacements up to 57 mum were achieved enabling adjustability of optical coupling efficiency

articleTitle: Titanium nitride micro-electromechanical bridge for wavelength selective switching
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: This paper reports on the use of titanium nitride (TiN) in a MEMS-based wavelength specific waveguide optical switch. By interfering a conductive MEMS bridge with the evanescent field of a ring resonator add/drop filter, the device can switch between enabling or disabling the ring resonator Problems with residual stresses in the MEMS bridges, leading to bridge deflection and thereby causing incomplete switching between the states, was addressed by the use of TiN as the MEMS bridge material. TiN has the virtue of being able to almost completely. We demonstrate the ability to virtually eliminate the residual stresses in TiN and thereby improve the bridge profile, promising much improved switching characteristics

articleTitle: A 3-D micromirror utilizing inverted-series-connected electrothermal bimorph actuators for piston and tilt motion
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: A new electrothermal micromirror with large piston and tilt motions was proposed and fabricated. Large initial tilt angles and optical path shifting of previously fabricated thermal micro mirrors were eliminated by employing inverted-series-connected (ISC) bimorph actuators

articleTitle: Deformable micro-mirror for adaptive optics composed of piezoelectric PZT thin films
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: In this paper we present the piezoelectric-driven deformable micro-mirror for optical wavefront correction. The mirror membrane was fabricated on diaphragm structure composed of piezoelectric PZT thin films on Si substrate. The application of voltage induced large deflection of the surface of the diaphragm

articleTitle: Development of a micro-electro-rnechanical deformable mirror for fiber laser emission modulation
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: We present the integration of deformable micro-mirror in switchable optical systems. The goal is to associate laser optics with the high and inexpensive replication of MEMS to create compact laser sources delivering intense pulsed radiation

articleTitle: Pull-in voltage measurements of torsional micromirror arrays for uniformity characterization
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS International Conference on Optical MEMS and Their Applications Conference, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we describe pull-in voltage measurement technique and results for the uniformity characterization of torsional micromirror arrays (MMAs). A simple measurement scheme using two illuminators and image processing was implemented. The MMAs were fabricated using two kinds of substrate; silicon on glass (SiOG) and silicon on insulator (SOI) wafers. Pull-in voltage distributions are presented, and the differences of two substrates on pull-in voltage distributions are compared
